local:depends-ban-is-now-a-choice-not-a-.title:
`hk.pkl` bans `depends` in favour of `exclusive = true` because a failed
dependency used to deadlock every dependent (`hk.pkl:152`, and the same doctrine
in `long-running-command-hangs.md` rule 5 + dotfiles' `no_hk_depends` step). The
trigger condition is `fail_fast = false` AND a step carrying `depends`. This
repo sets the first at `hk.pkl:12` and, because of this very ban, has ZERO of the
second — the only occurrence of `depends` in `hk.pkl` is the comment forbidding
it. So the deadlock could never have fired here; the ban is what made it
unreachable, which is the point rather than a caveat to it.

**Upstream FIXED it in v1.53.0 (#1099): dependents no longer hang after a failed
dependency.** So the ban is no longer a workaround for a live defect — it is a
choice, and `tool-currency-and-native-first.md` says custom avoidance kept alive
by a fixed defect is exactly what to re-examine.

Deliberately NOT retired (Ray, 2026-07-31): `exclusive` works, the doctrine spans
both repos, and dotfiles machine-enforces it — retiring it here alone would split
the two repos' rules. Recorded WITH its version condition so a future reader knows
which of the two it is, and so any revival is a decision rather than a rediscovery.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-03 for v1.54.0: unchanged in substance. 1.53.0 carried the
#1099 fix already recorded; 1.54.0 adds `check_failed_files`, command-effect
declarations and perf (17% smaller binary, 31% faster startup) with no
dependency-graph change. The ban stays a CHOICE, still deliberately not retired.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-08 for v1.54.1: unchanged in substance, and the release is
adjacent to this item without moving it. 1.54.1 is four bug fixes; the relevant
one (#1140) makes hk print an end-of-run hint on a git `index.lock` conflict
"pointing to `exclusive = true`, `depends`, or separate groups", and the docs
now steer authors toward `stage` for hk-owned staging and `exclusive` for
legacy commands that write the index directly. That is GUIDANCE, not a
dependency-graph change — upstream's own advice now names `exclusive` first,
which is what this repo already does. The ban stays a CHOICE, still
deliberately not retired.

local:hk-version-is-written-three-times.title:
dotfiles' `hk_version_parity` step does not port — it exists because
that repo carries THREE pkl files whose hk pins can drift apart, and this repo has
exactly ONE (`hk.pkl`, verified 2026-07-31).

But a drift surface remains on a DIFFERENT axis: the version appears three times
across two files — `mise.toml`'s `hk` pin, and `hk.pkl`'s `amends` and `import`
URLs. A `mise.toml`-only bump runs a new BINARY against the old SCHEMAS. Bump all
three together, or the mismatch shows up as a pkl error with nothing pointing at
the pin.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-03 at the 1.52.0 -> 1.54.0 bump, and the method held: the
version occurred exactly TWICE in `hk.pkl` (`amends` + `import`) and once in
`mise.toml`. All three moved in one edit, asserted on the count rather than
replaced blindly, then `hk validate` (rc=0) and `mise run lint` (rc=0) confirmed
the new binary agrees with the new schemas — which is this item's whole point.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-08 at the 1.54.0 -> 1.54.1 bump, and the method held again:
the version occurred exactly TWICE in `hk.pkl` (`amends` + `import`) and once in
`mise.toml`. Asserted on the count before editing (2, with a control of 0 for a
version not present), moved all three in one change, then `hk validate` rc=0 and
`mise run lint` rc=0 confirmed the new binary agrees with the new schemas.

NEW this round, and it is the failure this item exists to prevent wearing a
different hat: after `mise install`, a bare `hk` still ran **1.54.0** while
`mise which hk` reported 1.54.1. `MISE_ENV_CACHE=1` and the stale install dirs
sit at PATH positions 4/5/8, ahead of the shims. So "did the bump take?" cannot
be answered with `hk version`; use `mise exec -- hk version` or the absolute
path. The engine's own `resolution` check reports this independently.
